q: 1. The burning of bricks in kilns is complete within ..... hours.
explain: As per the answer key, burning in kilns is completed in about 24 hours.

q: 2. The bricks after burning in kilns require about ..... days to cool down for unloading.
explain: As per the answer key, bricks need about 12 days to cool down in the kiln before unloading.

q: 3. The bricks should be burnt at temperature from .....
explain: Good bricks are burnt at 1000°C to 1200°C so that the clay vitrifies and gains strength.

q: 4. The type of brick suitable for panel walls for multi-storeyed buildings is .....
explain: Hollow and perforated bricks are light, which reduces dead load on the frame, so both suit panel (non-load-bearing) walls.

q: 5. The compressive strength of perforated bricks should not be less than .....
explain: As per the answer key, the minimum compressive strength of perforated bricks is 7 MN/m².

q: 6. The compressive strength of paving bricks should not be less than .....
explain: Paving bricks must resist heavy wear and load, so the minimum compressive strength is 40 MN/m² as per the answer key.

q: 7. The length of a curved tile varies from .....
explain: As per the answer key, the length of a curved tile ranges from 15 to 20 cm.

q: 8. The dolomite bricks are .....
explain: Dolomite (calcium-magnesium carbonate) is basic in nature, so dolomite bricks are basic refractory bricks used in basic furnace linings.

q: 9. According to NS, in 1 cu. m. brick masonry, number of bricks required is
explain: As per standard practice for modular bricks, about 560 bricks are needed per cubic meter of masonry.

q: 10. Pick up the constituent of good brick earth whose excess causes the raw bricks shrink and warp during drying and burning, from the following
explain: Excess lime forms lumps that absorb moisture and expand on burning, causing bricks to crack and warp.

q: 11. Porcelain is used as
explain: Porcelain's smooth, non-porous, vitrified surface makes it the standard material for sanitary fittings.

q: 12. A 1st class brick immersed in water for 24 hours, should not absorb water (by weight) more than
explain: First class bricks must not absorb more than about 15% of their weight in water after 24-hour immersion.

q: 13. Sewer pipes are made of
explain: Stoneware is dense, vitrified, and chemically resistant, ideal for carrying sewage.

q: 14. Glazing of clay products, is done
options: to protect them from atmospheric effect
to protect them from corrosive action
explain: Glazing gives an impervious, attractive coating that protects clay products from weathering and corrosion.

q: 15. A pug mill is used for
explain: A pug mill kneads and tempers clay to a uniform, workable consistency free of air pockets before molding.

q: 16. Refractory bricks are used for .....
explain: Refractory bricks withstand very high temperatures, so they line furnaces and combustion chambers.

q: 17. The fire clay contains pure .....
explain: Fire clay consists mainly of hydrated aluminium silicate (alumina and silica), which gives it high heat resistance.

q: 18. Refractory bricks are .....
explain: Refractory bricks are classified as acid, basic and neutral types, so all the options are correct.

q: 19. Sewer pipes are made of .....
explain: Stoneware is hard, glazed and impervious, so it is used for sewer and drain pipes.

q: 20. The percentage of alumina and silica in good fire clay vary respectively is .....
explain: As per the answer key, good fire clay has about 25 to 30% alumina and 70 to 75% silica; option a matches.

q: 21. A bull nose brick is not used for .....
explain: Bull nose bricks have rounded edges for corners, pillars and decoration; arches use wedge-shaped (voussoir) bricks.

q: 22. Second class bricks .....
options: produce a metallic sound when struck
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Note: a metallic ringing sound is more typical of first class bricks, so this key answer is doubtful.

q: 23. Jhumb bricks are .....
explain: Jhamb (jhumb) bricks are over-burnt bricks that are irregular and vitrified.

q: 24. The portion of the brick cut across its width and having its length equal to that of a full brick, is known as .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b (queen closer).

q: 25. The indentation provided in a face of the brick is called
explain: The frog is the depression pressed into a brick's face, which helps key the brick to the mortar.

q: 26. The red color obtained by the bricks is due to the presence of
explain: Iron oxide in the clay oxidizes during burning, giving bricks their characteristic red color.

q: 27. The soil used for the manufacture of bricks should preferably not contain the following material
explain: Alkalies, pebbles, and kankar all cause defects (efflorescence, weak spots, unsoundness) and should be avoided in brick earth.

q: 28. Formation of whitish deposit on the bricks due to the presence of excess salts is called
explain: Efflorescence is the whitish deposit of soluble salts that migrate to the brick surface and crystallize as moisture evaporates.

q: 29. Ceramic material is manufactured from
options: natural clays and minerals admixture at high temperature
explain: Ceramics are inorganic, non-metallic materials processed by shaping and then firing at high temperatures (vitrification).

q: 30. The nature of ceramic material is
explain: Ceramics are characterized by high hardness and high resistance to heat, but they lack ductility and fail suddenly (brittle).

q: 31. The nature of refractories material is
explain: Refractory materials are designed to withstand high temperatures and often require low porosity to resist chemical attack.

q: 32. Refractory bricks are specially manufactured
options: to have high insulation against sound
explain: Refractory bricks, also known as fire bricks, are designed to resist high temperatures (up to 1700°C) without melting or softening.

q: 33. The soil good for making bricks is
explain: Clayey soil is ideal because it provides the necessary plasticity for molding and strength after burning.

q: 34. The impurity not desirable in the soil used for brick formation is
explain: Alkalis cause efflorescence (white staining), while Kankar (lime nodules) can cause bricks to split upon hydration.

q: 35. The ingredient of the brick earth which enables the brick to retain shape is
explain: Silica prevents the brick from warping, shrinking, and cracking; it provides the 'skeleton' for shape retention.

q: 36. The maximum percentage of ingredients in brick formation is
explain: Silica (sand) constitutes the largest portion of brick earth, typically ranging from 50% to 60%.

q: 37. The red colour of the brick is due to
explain: Iron oxide (roughly 5-6%) acts as a flux and imparts the characteristic red color to the brick upon burning.

q: 38. The standard size of a brick as per Nepal Standard (NS) is
explain: The Nepal Standard (NS) specifies the brick size as 230mm x 115mm x 57mm.

q: 39. Swelling of bricks is known as
explain: Bloating refers to the swelling/blistering of bricks, often caused by overburning or gas formation during firing.

q: 40. For what purpose are fire bricks used
options: to protect the building against lightening
explain: Fire bricks are used to line furnaces/kilns, insulating structures by decreasing heat flow while withstanding high temperatures.

q: 41. The percentage of alumina in good brick earth lies between
explain: Alumina is responsible for plasticity and should be between 20-30% of the brick earth volume.

q: 42. Excess of silica in brick earth causes
explain: While silica is vital, an excess makes the brick brittle and weak because it destroys the cohesion between soil particles.

q: 43. Excess of alumina in a brick earth causes
explain: Excess alumina makes the clay too plastic, leading to significant shrinkage, cracking, and warping during the drying and burning process.

q: 44. The size of modular bricks, is .....
explain: The standard modular brick is 19 × 9 × 9 cm (19.0 cm length, and with mortar 20 × 10 × 10 cm).

q: 45. The main function of alumina in brick earth is
explain: Alumina absorbs water and renders the clay plastic, which is essential for the molding of the brick.

q: 46. The term frog means .....
options: an apparatus to lift the stone
a depression on a face of brick
vertical joint in a brick work
explain: A frog is the depression on a face of the brick that holds mortar for a better key.

q: 47. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make brick is called
explain: Tempering is the process of adding water to the brick earth and kneading it to achieve a uniform, plastic mass.

q: 48. Which of the following ingredients of the brick earth enables the brick to retain its shape?
explain: Silica prevents cracking, shrinkage and warping and helps the brick retain its shape.

q: 49. Excess of iron oxide in brick earth causes
options: the colour change i.e. from red to dark blue
explain: While iron oxide provides the red color, an excess amount during burning causes the brick to turn dark blue or blackish.

q: 50. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make brick is known as .....
explain: As per the answer key, kneading. Note: other questions in the book use 'pugging' or 'tempering' for the same operation.
